picks.headline: Patriots-Jets Week 6 preview: Keys to victory, prediction and more
picks.blurb: Patriots-Jets Week 6 preview: Keys to victory, prediction and more – NBC Sports Boston Celtics New England seeks its third straight win. By Justin Leger • Published 1 hour ago • Updated 1 hour ago Nov 13, 2025; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) looks to pass the ball against the New York Jets in the first quarter at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images The New England Patriots snapped out of their early-season funk with back-to-back impressive wins over the Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders. Will they stay hot this Sunday against the New York Jets? If Drake Maye plays how he has over the last two weeks, the Jets won't stand much of a chance. The third-year quarterback is back to looking like his MVP-caliber self. He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week after a 269-yard, three-TD performance vs. Buffalo, and should've earned the honor again after his 374-yard, five-TD gem against Vegas. The Patriots have dominated the Jets for the last two-and-a-half decades, but don't underestimate New York heading into this Week 6 matchup. Its pass defense has been among the NFL's best so far this season, so it won't be easy for Maye to keep his torrid stretch going, even if star wide receiver A.J. Brown is back in the mix. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels may have to lean more on the run game, which would mean a heavy workload for Rhamondre Stevenson with TreVeyon Henderson likely out with an ankle injury . As of Thursday, New England is a 7.5-point favorite to win Sunday's game at Gillette Stadium. What are the keys to matching those expectations? Here's our Pats-Jets Week 6 preview and prediction: Recent head-to-head matchups The Patriots beating up on the Jets is a tradition like no other. They've won 40 of their last 50 regular-season games against their storied AFC East rival since December 2001. They've lost to New York only twice in the last decade. Last season, the Patriots took care of business with a 13-point win at home before blowing the Jets out at MetLife Stadium. Here are the last three Patriots-Jets matchups: Week 11, 2025 at New England: 27-14 Patriots Week 17, 2025 at New York: 42-10 Patriots Week 8, 2024 at New England: 25-22 Patriots View this post on Instagram Key Stats David Bailey is a game-wrecker Jets edge rusher David Bailey could be a problem for the Patriots on Sunday. Bailey has five sacks through the first five weeks of his NFL career, including three in New York's 17-12 win over Cleveland last week. The undrafted rookie also racked up three tackles for loss and four total QB hits to earn the AFC Defensive Player of the Week honor. According to the NFL, Bailey became the first rookie since Jean Phillips with at least three sacks and three TFLs in the same game. David Bailey was a man on a mission in Week 5 🔥 @Pepsi https://t.co/DKOYWjlsLg Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is well-aware of the challenge Bailey presents. "He's fast, explosive, instinctive," Vrabel said of Bailey on Wednesday. "He can bend, got a really good get off and is able to win at the top and corner. He uses his get off, so just like every week, we'll have to be very conscious of the front." Feed Rhamondre? The Jets have had one of the stingiest pass defenses this season, limiting opponents to an average of 175 passing yards per game (fourth-fewest in NFL). They could make it tough for Maye to push the ball downfield, giving McDaniels no choice but to lean on his running backs. That means we should expect a hefty workload for Rhamondre Stevenson. The Pats' RB2, TreVeyon Henderson, will miss time after suffering a high-ankle sprain last week. Stevenson and Corey Kiner are the only RBs currently on the active roster, though Lan Larison and Hassan Haskins are candidates to be elevated from the practice squad. While the Jets aren't terrible against the run, they're beatable. They rank 13th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (118). Patriots' key to victory Protect Drake Maye The Jets are tied for third in the NFL with 17 sacks this season. As mentioned above, rookie edge rusher David Bailey leads the group with five sacks, three coming last week vs. Cleveland. The Patriots offensive line will be tested against this menacing Jets front, especially if left tackle Will Campbell is out due to the knee injury he suffered last week. "I think they're physical. I think they have tenacity. I think they've got, I wouldn't say a new ferociousness, but you can see the difference on tape from last year," Maye said of the Jets defense on Wednesday. "They have some new faces, some new mentality. I think they're buying into how Coach [Aaron] Glenn wants to play defense, and I think you respect that. "You can see that on film. It pops out to you. They do a good job on the back end, mixing it up and also getting on you and grabbing you and playing physical. So, you can see that they're building something on defense, and it's really shown this year with how they played. Maye struggled mightily over the first three weeks of the season. Uncoincidentally, he was pressured often and sacked nine times in that span. Over his last two stellar games, Maye has only been sacked twice. Jets' key to victory Win the turnover battle The only way we see the Patriots losing to the Jets at home this week is if they fail to protect the football. That's how they earned both of their losses this season, with Maye tossing three interceptions in the season opener vs. Seattle and turning it over four times in Week 3 against Jacksonville. Fortunately for Maye and the Pats, the Jets don't pick anyone off. They went a record 21 games without an interception before safety Minkah Fitzpatrick finally snapped the streak in Week 4. That was New York's only INT so far this year. Fumbles are a different story. The Jets are tied for second in the NFL with five fumble recoveries this season. Maye has fumbled five times, Stevenson lost a fumble in Week 2, and Kiner coughed it up in last week's win. The Patriots must avoid giving the Jets extra possessions. If they do that, they should win this game pretty handily. Over the last two weeks, the Pats have resembled the 2025 team that finished 14-3 and represented the AFC in the Super Bowl. If they're even 75 percent as good as they were against Buffalo and Las Vegas, they should breeze past New York at home. That said, the Jets defense is capable of keeping this one close, especially if key Pats players are sidelined due to injuries. Running back TreVeyon Henderson and left tackle Will Campbell are expected to be out, and it remains to be seen whether star wideout A.J. Brown is ready to return from injured reserve. This could be a tougher matchup than many anticipate. But even if the Patriots are forced to embrace the "next man up" mentality yet again, a decent performance from Maye should be enough to propel them to 4-2. away.headline: New York Jets' Blitz Rate Is a Risk Against Patriots QB Drake Maye
away.blurb: The potential return of Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) raises the stakes. Locked On Patriots host Nick Cattles said Brown had returned to practice after the team opened his 21-day window, though his availability and workload remained unclear. Butchko said Brown’s presence would force the Jets to alter their coverage approach even if he plays a limited role because New York lacks the true shutdown corner it once had with Sauce Gardner. – Tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) returned to practice in a limited capacity, according to Butchko. He argued the Jets need to simplify the rookie’s role and create more intermediate-field opportunities if he is cleared, particularly with Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell expected to miss the game. The New York Jets may need to abandon the volume of defensive pressure that helped them beat Cleveland when they visit the New England Patriots on Sunday. Locked On Jets host John Butchko pointed to New York’s blitz rate in Week 5 and argued that repeatedly sending extra rushers at Patriots quarterback Drake Maye would leave the Jets liable to big plays. (Butchko referred to the blitz rate as 47%, but TruMedia listed it as 52.3%.) Butchko said Maye’s mobility and success against pressure make this a different assignment from the rain-soaked matchup against the Browns. The Jets can still create a turnover by disguising pressure and picking their spots, but an overemphasis on the blitz would give Maye chances to extend plays and attack openings in the secondary. A more selective rush would put greater responsibility on the secondary to cover longer, especially if Brown is active. The Jets have received better-than-expected early contributions from cornerbacks Azareye’h Thomas and Brandon Stephens, plus safety Dane Belton, but Maye presents a more demanding test when he can escape the initial pressure. The counterargument is clear: Sitting back too often could give Maye a clean pocket and allow the Patriots to sustain their explosive-play offense. New York’s answer may be to vary its looks rather than make pressure the defining feature of every passing down. For a defense that has protected its red zone well, preventing a few vertical completions could matter more than chasing sacks. The Jets have a path to a second straight win if they make Maye work through tight windows, limit the Patriots’ explosive plays and avoid letting one coverage bust turn an aggressive call into a momentum swing. – Wide receiver Garrett Wilson will draw a major individual test from Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), who returned to practice after missing the past two games. Campbell is now considered "week-to-week" as the Patriots prepare for this coming Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the division-rival New York Jets. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said of Campbell's injury status on Monday. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. We’ll take it day by day and see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday, and keep you updated on the injury report.” After a slow start to the 2026 season, the Patriots are beginning to catch their stride. Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders marked the team's second consecutive victory and third win of the season thus far. Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Jets will kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

home.headline: New York Jets' Blitz Rate Is a Risk Against Patriots QB Drake Maye
home.blurb: The potential return of Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) raises the stakes. Locked On Patriots host Nick Cattles said Brown had returned to practice after the team opened his 21-day window, though his availability and workload remained unclear. Butchko said Brown’s presence would force the Jets to alter their coverage approach even if he plays a limited role because New York lacks the true shutdown corner it once had with Sauce Gardner. – Tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) returned to practice in a limited capacity, according to Butchko. He argued the Jets need to simplify the rookie’s role and create more intermediate-field opportunities if he is cleared, particularly with Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell expected to miss the game. The New York Jets may need to abandon the volume of defensive pressure that helped them beat Cleveland when they visit the New England Patriots on Sunday. Locked On Jets host John Butchko pointed to New York’s blitz rate in Week 5 and argued that repeatedly sending extra rushers at Patriots quarterback Drake Maye would leave the Jets liable to big plays. (Butchko referred to the blitz rate as 47%, but TruMedia listed it as 52.3%.) Butchko said Maye’s mobility and success against pressure make this a different assignment from the rain-soaked matchup against the Browns. The Jets can still create a turnover by disguising pressure and picking their spots, but an overemphasis on the blitz would give Maye chances to extend plays and attack openings in the secondary. A more selective rush would put greater responsibility on the secondary to cover longer, especially if Brown is active. The Jets have received better-than-expected early contributions from cornerbacks Azareye’h Thomas and Brandon Stephens, plus safety Dane Belton, but Maye presents a more demanding test when he can escape the initial pressure. The counterargument is clear: Sitting back too often could give Maye a clean pocket and allow the Patriots to sustain their explosive-play offense. New York’s answer may be to vary its looks rather than make pressure the defining feature of every passing down. For a defense that has protected its red zone well, preventing a few vertical completions could matter more than chasing sacks. The Jets have a path to a second straight win if they make Maye work through tight windows, limit the Patriots’ explosive plays and avoid letting one coverage bust turn an aggressive call into a momentum swing. – Wide receiver Garrett Wilson will draw a major individual test from Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), who returned to practice after missing the past two games. Ed Valentine Thu, October 15, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Can the New York Giants, 3-0 at MetLife Stadium this season, continue their winning ways at home on Sunday when they face the New Orleans Saints? Below, how the Big Blue View staff is predicting the game, as well as the rest of the NFL Week 6 action. Just how beaten up are the Giants? That's the question on my mind as we get ready for this game. I think I'm less concerned with Abdul Carter than I am with Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor. Even though Thomas hasn't been healthy since Week 1, the Giants have still fielded one of the very best tackle duos in the NFL. And while Marcus Mbow has played well in his outing, he's struggled with power in the past. That's a bit of a concern given the Saints have a pair of good-sized and powerful defensive ends in Chase Young and Carl Granderson. That said, the Saints' defense has been pretty porous and their win rates haven't been great this year. As long as the Giants can protect Jameis Winston, there should be opportunities to move the ball and score. On the flip side, the Giants' defense has been playing with a similar aggression as the Vikings' defense that held Tyler Shough to 3.8 yards per attempt, and their offense to 142 total yards. The Giants' pass rush has been dynamic over the last two games, and they've been opportunistic in creating turnovers. The Giants' athletic blitzers could cause many of the same problems for the Saints as the Vikings' did — at least assuming Abdul Carter's calf injury is minor. I'm still going to pick the Giants to win the game, but my confidence level depends on the the Giants' health. Tony Del Genio This is an uncomfortable matchup for the Giants. The Saints have been sub-.500 in three of the past four seasons, yet they have beaten the Giants three years in a row. The Giants' last victory was in overtime in 2021, when Daniel Jones passed for 402 yards in the Superdome. The losing quarterback in that game was…Jameis Winston. History aside, my discomfort stems from what I see as a non-ideal matchup of strengths and weaknesses. Tyler Shough is a very experienced quarterback even though this is only his second year in the NFL. His receiving corps is better than what the Giants saw last week, most notably Chris Olave, second in the NFL in receiving yards. Shough was flummoxed by Brian Flores' blitzing Minnesota defense last week. If that sounds like good news because Dennard Wilson has become fond of the blitz himself, it's not. Flores' defense works because the zone defense and deception he uses behind it induce quarterbacks to throw quickly to receivers they think are open, but aren't. Dennard instead is playing a decent amount of Cover 0 and leaving cornerbacks to stay with receivers in single coverage. Can the Giants' cornerbacks cover receivers like Olave? The answer to that may decide the game. I'm more optimistic about the Giants on offense…if they can protect Winston. Chase Young is back to his early form, and with Carl Granderson on the other side form a good 1-2 punch against…whom? Neither Andrew Thomas nor Jermaine Eluemunor practiced on Wednesday. If Winston sees a lot of pressure, it could be lights out for the Giants. Given time, though, he may be able to exploit the Saints' second and third levels. And maybe the Giants can find a way to finally run the ball effectively against one of the worst run defenses in the league. I choose to be optimistic this week. A little, anyway. David Hartman I'm more than a little surprised that the 1-4 Saints are favored over the 3-1-1 Giants this Sunday, and especially with the game being played at MetLife. Then again, while the Giants are 2-0-1 in their last three outings, all of those games were effectively decided on the final play of the game. New York is a bounce (and brain fart) or two away from also being 1-4. The Saints are Big Blue's fourth straight opponent who, like them, picked in the Top-10 of the 2026 draft, with three of those four games at home. This game is the end of the easy stretch of New York's schedule. New Orleans can throw the ball, but they can't run it or stop the run. They rank 30th in the NFL in rushing offense and 29th in rushing defense. Kellen Moore's offense is fast-paced — they're second in the league in plays per game (74). Dennard Wilson's defense will need to stay fresh, and play better than it did last week against Washington. Sustained drives by New York's offense should help with that. I like the Giants to win fairly convincingly in this one, and for the first time in a month, I don't think you'll need to wear a heart monitor to watch the fourth quarter. They should be able to establish the run and work some play-action off of that, and I think they'll be able to rattle Tyler Shough with their pass rush, as the Vikings did last week. Jameis Winston didn't throw any picks last week (although he did lose a fumble) and while it's a lot to ask for a repeat, I think he's showing pretty good command and very good rapport with his main weapons. They'll get a lift from the home crowd too. The Giants come home Sunday to face a the New Orleans Saints, a team that has been put on notice by their owner just this week that improvements are needed. I do not know about you, but when my boss tells me something like that, my work goes up a notch. As Jon Runyan noted this week, the Giants could easily be 1-4 and they are a beat up team coming off their tie in Washington— there is a real chance that their offensive tackles could be a first- and second-year player at some point on Sunday. When teams are evenly matched, I always go with the more desperate team and the Giants using up all of their luck last week. Pick: Saints 27, Giants 10 Valentine's View Like others above, this game makes be a bit queasy from a Giants' perspective. They have lost to the Saints three years in a row. The 1-4 Saints are likely better than their record, and are under fire from ownership . They will come to MetLife Stadium desperate to turn their season around. The Giants are 3-0 at home this season, but you are fooling yourself if you think they will win every game at MetLife. The Saints are vulnerable defensively and middling offensively, but the Giants have plenty of their own issues. I think the Giants can find a way to win this game. Perhaps that comes down to the belief in themselves the Giants have developed vs. a Saints team that has underperformed expectations. I feel like, at least for now, things have been bouncing the Giants way. If Abdul Carter can't play, though, my view on this game might change. Giants fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! The Giants tied with the Washington Commanders in what ended up being one of the weirder games of the season. New York should have lost to Washington, so the fact that they tied is being taken as a win for the team. But the Giants know that they will need a better effort going forward this week as the team gets ready to face off against the New Orleans Saints at home. New Orleans will be coming into the game looking to stop the bleeding, with the Saints sitting with a record of 1-4 on the year. Both sides need a win this week for different reasons, and the Giants will try to remain perfect at home this season. New York can't overlook this Saints team despite their struggles this season; otherwise, the Giants could find themselves in a tight contest. Bleacher Report did game predictions for every contest this week, with Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford picking. In these predictions, every single expert went with the Giants to take down New Orleans. Much of this could be due to the Saints having their own problems this year, but the Giants have shown real promise as a team. Even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart going down with an injury, the Giants have been able to stay the course. Backup signal-caller Jameis Winston has held down the fort well for New York, showing that he can get this team to the playoffs. But the problem with Winston is that he has been very inconsistent over the years in his career, and the Giants know this from the first few weeks of the season. As he gets ready to face off against New Orleans, Winston will need to make sure to stay focused. Winston can be very turnover-prone at times, and the Giants can't afford any issues against the Saints this week. The Giants defense has been a calling card for the team this season, helping them win a few games. And going against an explosive Saints passing attack, the New York secondary will need to be ready to go. picks.headline: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants
picks.blurb: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Lorenzo Styles Jr. #36 of the New Orleans Saints plays against the Minnesota Vikings during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads I want to start this week's report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don't disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this class from doing much, but you shouldn't lose faith in this group. The players who have been in the game have made plays that are good starting points, and although development matters, it's not like those players have been bad. Jordyn Tyson's injury is annoying to say the least, but hopefully we can forget about that once he's back. Do I think this class is going to be like 2025? No, but in hindsight, I think he could be a nice, middle-of-the-road draft class. Now onto the players: DT Christen Miller Finally, Christen Miller was able to get into the game on Sunday, and eventhough the Saints could not win, he did well in his short time. Miller made big plays against the run, took up blocks from offensive linemen to open up holes for other defensive linemen and the linebackers to stop the run, and in my opinion, proved he should be the starting nose tackle. It wasn't perfect, but it was enough for the Saints to play him more. This should hopefully be the case against the New York Giants, and to stop RB Cam Skattebo, you need a big defensive lineman that can prevent him from carrying the pile. TE Oscar Delp With the Vikings sending blitzes nearly every play, Delp had to step up as a blocker, and he did. The Giants are also at the top of the league in blitz rate, so Delp will be a primary blocker once again. I do hope the Saints utilize him as a receiver, because Noah Fant has had pre-snap issues this season, and prioritizing youth should be the plan moving forward. Try something new. OG Jeremiah Wright Speaking of trying something new, I wish Jeremiah Wright would get some snaps, but now that pressure is on the organization to win, a Cesar Ruiz trade feels less likely due to the risk. If a coaching change is made, I hope the next staff will give Wright a chance. WR Bryce Lance Last week, I said that it's clear Lance is not ready for WR3, and the Vikings game only reinforced that. The Saints need to make the move and put him at WR4 moving forward so he can learn. I know I have said to prioritize youth, but I also want to prioritize Tyler Shough's development, and Lance is negatively affecting that. WR Barion Brown Brown is a similar spot to Lance, but it's also clear he needs to figure out the return game as well. His fellow former LSU Tiger, Zavion Thomas, is in nearly the exact same spot with the Bears, but due to their offensive struggles with Caleb Williams being out, they have begun to utilize Thomas more. In addition, Thomas has improved as their main return man. Hopefully, the same can happen for Brown. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson was thrown to the wolves trying to block the Vikings blitz, and although I felt he did a decent job, he did have a holding call on one of the plays. As a rusher, Donaldson did exactly what I thought, picking up tough yards that did help the Saints in their run game. Against the Giants, I want him to be included once again. OT Mason Murphy In probably the most confusing moment of the game, which is saying a lot, the Saints put in Mason Murphy on a random drive, then subbed him out for Asim Richards the next. At first, I thought Richards got injured, but Moore said after the game that it was planned. I actually thought Richards did better than usual, and Murphy wasn't great when he came in. I don't think the Saints will make this substitution again. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was back last game, which was nice to see, but his involvement was limited. I wouldn't be shocked if that changes after Jayden Price's release being cut, so Styles Jr. could be the return man next to Brown against the Giants. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson

away.headline: Saints WR Chris Olave appears on injury report with new issue
away.blurb: Olave took the field for practice in a limited capacity on Thursday, but a new “foot” designation was added to the report. While this “foot” designation could be cause for concern, the fact that Olave took the field for a limited practice is a positive sign for his Week 5 status. New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave did not participate in Wednesday’s Week 5 practice session, landing on the injury report with a “rest” designation. This new issue comes as a surprise to fans and reporters who saw Olave take a hit to the knee late in Monday night’s matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. Trailing 45-17 with just over one minute remaining in the primetime contest, the superstar wide receiver limped off the field with what was assumed to be a knee injury. Olave ranks second in NFL receiving yards so far this season with 491, trailing only Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (498). He recorded his third 100+ receiving yard game of the year in Monday’s loss to the Falcons, reeling in eight receptions for 116 yards. The 1-3 Saints will welcome the Minnesota Vikings for a Week 5 matchup this coming Sunday. away.headline: Vikings-Saints Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, some intrigue with a number of players listed as questionable, including Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, and Brian O’Neill. I’m gonna go out on a limb and say that all three will play on Sunday. I know they will be cautious with all of them, but it doesn’t sound like Jefferson has experienced any problems with his ankle all week. It sounds like Addison and O’Neill’s injuries are more of the minor variety they will play through. It’s not a surprise at this point that Christian Darrisaw is out, as he hadn’t practiced all week. He should be ready to go after the bye week. For the Saints, Alvin Kamara is questionable but my guess is he’ll play on Sunday. Safety Julian Blackmon is also questionable but probably will play as well. Those are the two key players on the Saints list this week. Everyone else is either listed as out or do not have a deisignation and/or are a backup. Who will be sitting this one out? away.headline: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve
away.blurb: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Caleb's return won't solve it all New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve Welcome back, Zach Wood. The New Orleans Saints long snapper was a full participant at practice on Wednesday, marking his return from injured reserve. He'll need to continue practicing throughout the week in order to be activated for Sunday's game with the New York Giants , but all signs point to him snapping the ball at MetLife Stadium. The Saints released fill-in long snapper Cal Adomitis and don't have another player at the position on their roster. They also left a vacancy open and waiting for Wood on the 53-man roster once he gets the green light. Wood, 33, won the job back in 2017 and was the long snapper for New Orleans in 150 consecutive regular season games (plus seven playoff games), finally ending his streak when a calf strain forced him out of action the last four weeks. The fear was that he would have needed even more time to recover, but he's ahead of schedule and expected to be back in the lineup. Wood has made quite a career for himself as a former rookie free agent out of SMU. He actually spent some time with the Dallas Cowboys when Kellen Moore was the backup quarterback in 2016 and part of the 2017 preseason. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve John Sigler, Saints Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:56 AM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads He's been missed. Adomitis had some hiccups and drew an untimely penalty during Week 5's loss to the Minnesota Vikings , so getting Wood back on the field should help steady the operation. You just hope he isn't rushing himself back too soon.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. However, Wednesday night's follow-up ultrasound showed movement in the clot, prompting the Eagles to rule him out while determining the appropriate treatment. "Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment," the Eagles said. "His health and safety are our highest priority." Pro Football Doc Injury Analysis: How Long Could Jalen Hurts Be Out? A major factor in Hurts' return timeline will be whether he requires anticoagulants, commonly known as blood thinners. Chao noted that playing football while taking these medications creates a significant bleeding risk, particularly with head injuries. The best-case scenario would involve no further clot progression, no need for blood thinners and a return as soon as Week 7. However, Chao does not consider that the most likely outcome. Running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith have both missed time with hamstring injuries and did not practice Wednesday ahead of Week 6. According to an official statement from the Eagles, Hurts initially injured his calf when he was cleated during Philadelphia's October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. Hurts first sought treatment Thursday, October 8, after practicing Wednesday and Thursday fully. He received additional treatment Friday and was added to the injury report despite another full practice. An ultrasound performed Saturday after the team arrived in London revealed a superficial blood clot. After reviewing the results, team doctors determined that Hurts could safely play, with activity and mobility considered important. Hurts played without limitations Sunday and received treatment Monday and Tuesday before practicing fully on Wednesday. According to Pro Football Doc, Dr. David Chao, Hurts' superficial blood clot is different from deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a potentially more dangerous condition involving a clot in a deeper vein. Chao explained that superficial blood clots can progress into deeper veins, making further evaluation important. The Eagles must determine whether the clot resulted from the initial cleat injury, prolonged inactivity during travel or another underlying issue. Chao expects Hurts to miss multiple weeks , although the timeline could extend significantly if anticoagulation or additional treatment is necessary. Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons (+3) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one. Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense. Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3) Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it. Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-13.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day. Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20 Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye. Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21 Buffalo Bills (-6) at Las Vegas Raiders The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills. Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Week 6 Tracker: Injury updates, predictions, storylines and more
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Week 6 Tracker: Injury updates, predictions, storylines and more - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Pittsburgh Steelers RB Jaylen Warren (L) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. (R) | Lauren Leigh Bacho and Perry Knotts - Getty Images | Graphic by Adam Patrick Shayne Kubas Wed, October 14, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Coming off their thrilling 34-22 home victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5, the 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers head south this week to face the 1-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who themselves are coming off their first win of the season last week against the Dallas Cowboys. Despite their record (and an injury to starting quarterback Baker Mayfield), the Bucs are coming off their two most competitive games of the season, with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels filling in for Mayfield. It looks as though Daniels will once again be the one under center against Pittsburgh, and they can't allow him to look nearly as comfortable as Dallas did a week ago. Tampa Bay and Pittsburgh haven't played each other many times, but the Steelers have dominated those meetings 10-2. To keep pace in a hotly contested AFC North, they badly need that to become 11-2 this weekend. Everything you could want to know about this matchup, including injury updates, weather forecasts, storylines, and more, can be found right here. So make sure to bookmark this page and come back throughout the week. How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6 Date: Sunday, October 18 Time: 1:00 p.m. EST TV Network: CBS Announcers: Andrew Catalon (Play-by-Play), Logan Ryan (Color Analyst), AJ Ross (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 6 Steelers injury reports will be available here once they are released, beginning Wednesday, October 14 Tampa Bay Buccaneers Injury Report for Week 6 Buccaneers injury reports will be available here once they are released, beginning Wednesday, October 14 Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs Tampa Buccaneers Week 6 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: 79 degrees Wind Speed: 20 mph Precipitation: Isolated Rain Showers Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 6 Can Jaylen Warren keep up his unbelievable run against a tough Tampa run defense? Calling what Jaylen Warren has done over the past three games "unbelievable may not be the right word, since many Steelers fans have seen glimpses of the level of play he's reached this season. Still, three consecutive games with over 125 yards from scrimmage is no small feat. In fact, Warren is the only player to do that so far this season. The Buccaneers will be his toughest test so far by a mile; however, they are allowing just 3.28 yards per attempt on the ground, according to Sumer Sports . If Warren can maintain his level of production against a tough opponent like Tampa Bay, then his breakout will feel even more real than it already does. Can the Steelers' run defense shut down another high-powered run game? No Derrick Harmon, no problem for the Steelers in Week 5 against the Colts' rushing attack. Despite facing star running back Jonathan Taylor, Pittsburgh completely shut down the run against Indianapolis. They allowed just 66 yards on 24 attempts for a measly 2.8 yards per carry. While Harmon's absence didn't hurt them last week, the Buccaneers' run game has actually been more efficient than the Colts' this year, even before the Steelers crushed them a week ago. Bucky Irving looks much more like the player who burst onto the scene as a rookie in 2024, increasing his yards-per-attempt average from 3.4 last season to 5.3 so far this year. If Pittsburgh can slow him down with Harmon still on Injured Reserve, it should give the unit a ton of confidence moving forward. Will Tampa Bay play more man coverage, and can the Steelers handle it if they do? The Steelers' offense looks much better over the past three games after struggling mightily to start the season, but their kryptonite has remained the same for most of their five games: man coverage. Pittsburgh's receivers simply aren't winning often enough when teams man them up, and Aaron Rodgers' unwillingness to stay calm in the pocket isn't exactly helping either. The old gunslinger can still carve up zone for the most part, but unless his receivers can win almost immediately against man, he simply doesn't have the same playmaking ability he once had. Tampa Bay has played man on just 19.1% of their snaps this season, according to Sumer Sports. Will that change against Pittsburgh? And if it does, can they find success despite being down three receivers? Speaking of... Will the Steelers' offense change at all with multiple receivers now on the shelf? Pittsburgh will head into Week 6 down three receivers : Roman Wilson, Michael Pittman Jr., and special teams ace Ben Skowronek. For a team that wants to live in 11 personnel and in the shotgun, it could mean a serious change in how they operate until at least one of them returns. Pittsburgh shifted to more 12 and 22 personnel in the second half of Week 5 once Wilson and Skowronek went down, but will that plan carry over into next week? It's hard to say for sure given how Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy prefer to run the offense, but I certainly hope they are smart enough to lean on their tight ends and running backs without their full group of playmakers available. Even when everyone has been healthy, they have been far more effective when using heavier formations, so the offense may actually be in a better situation despite the unfortunate injuries. Todd Bowles and his pewter pirates managed to pull out a sensationally shocking upset of the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Behind the mighty galloping of Bucky Irving and the poise of UDFA Jalen Daniels, Tampa's marauders took over AT&T Stadium. This Sunday (for the third week in a row), it'll be another classic blueblood NFL franchise on the schedule for the Buccaneers— The Pittsburgh Steelers. "The offense can't score if they don't have the ball." How can the Buccaneers win? ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bucs need to make sure they stay on schedule and stick to their gameplan. There are NFL teams that have the benefit of being able to get into different types of games and win in a variety of ways— The Buccaneers are not that team. If a win is in the cards, they need to make sure they are playing the hand that best suits them. Last week, in Dallas, Tampa did a phenomenal job of staying in the realm of football that they themselves are comfortable playing. The Buccaneers kept the ball on the ground, dominated time of possession— Starting with a 10-minute opening drive, and kept Dallas off-kilter. That dictation was not only an advantage for Tampa Bay, it's the reason they won. That in turn made the Cowboys play the game the Buccaneers needed to play, not the one Dallas wanted to play. It would be easy to say, 'If Bucky Irving rushes for nearly 200 yards, the Buccaneers have a good chance of winning' , but it's more than the yards on the stat sheet. Irving's performance was eye-popping, but it was the offense's ability to stay on the field that won Tampa Bay the game. The Buccaneers finished the game with just shy of 40 minutes time of possession, while Dallas' heralded offense held the ball for just 20. That discrepancy is catastrophic for any team to be on the wrong side of— Personified through the consistent cutaways by Amazon's broadcast as they kept showing defeated, disengaged, and dispirited Dallas Cowboys on the sideline. Consecutive weeks with 40 minutes of possession may not be on the docket, however, will the Buccaneers' offense be able to keep themselves steady, avoid turnovers, and push Pittsburgh to play the type of game Tampa wants to play? "The question isn't who is going to let me; it's who is going to stop me." How can the Buccaneers lose? The Steelers have had some inconsistent offense this year, but they've had 24-plus points in each of the last three weeks (30, 24, 34). Of course, they can't score if they don't play (See the above portion of this article). The Buccaneers' second best option for keeping Pittsburgh's points down, besides pilfering clock, is turnovers. Tampa's turnover differential on the season is not glamourous (-2). Maybe even more absurd, that hideous -2 sits boldly after the Bucs just had a +3 in their last contest. Aside from points themselves, nothing has ever been, or will ever be, a more clear determinant of wins and losses than turnovers. Teams that take the ball away win a lot more than teams that lose the ball. Having the ball means having more chances to score, more chances to score means more better odds you will score; ergo, turnovers are good. More importantly, for a struggling, very one-dimensional team like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, turnovers level the playing field. The scenario is two-fold. Not only does it fall on your defense to force them, but your offense must avoid turnovers like a coach on the hot seat must avoid losing. Last week, Tampa hit the trifecta— Their defense (and special teams) took the ball away from Dallas three times. Jalen Daniels and the Bucs' offense did not turn the ball over at all and their coach on the heat seat avoided a loss. This week, it's not Dak Prescott it's Aaron Rodgers. Aaron Rodgers is a historically anti-turnover prone quarterback. The former Packers' legend, Jets' bust, and current Steelers' stopgap, has quite literally the greatest touchdown to interception ratio in NFL history— As in, number one. Rodgers is not the type of quarterback that you want to face if the gameplan is get the ball— however , against all odds, Tampa Bay's ever assailed head coach Todd Bowles has actually had a healthy level of success against Rodgers during his Bucs' tenure. The two haven't matched up since Rodgers left Green Bay, but the duels have actually largely favored Bowles. In three games versus Todd Bowles' Tampa Bay defense, Rodgers has a losing record and has looked extremely ordinary. The four-time NFL MVP has wracked up just five touchdowns and he's also tossed four interceptions. The backdrop is laid out much differently for the 2026 edition, Rodgers has a new team, a new (his old) coach, is playing at a completely different level (which may actually further favor Bowles), and Bowles does not have nearly the same defensive firepower he once did. Sunday, will likely be the last time the two battle— A final chapter in the story. The storylines for Sunday's Bowles-Rodgers epilogue, can Todd Bowles get him again? Rodgers has yet to play a clean game against Bowles' Bucs. Will the Buccaneers' offense be able to stay mistake free for a second straight week? Turnovers, like they had against Rodgers' former team two weeks ago, will almost assuredly sink them into a self-dug 1-5 hole.

away.headline: Steelers' young defender dealing with surprise ankle injury ahead of Week 6
away.blurb: Courtesy of the team's initial injury report for the Week 6 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Steelers defensive lineman Keeanu Benton was listed as a non-participant with a surprising ankle injury. It's unclear when Benton suffered the injury, but it's believed to have been during the Week 5 win over the Colts . Benton was able to return to practice on Thursday as a limited participant, but it's a concerning development nonetheless. Benton, who was drafted in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft, hasn't quite lived up to his new $72 million extension through five games this season. Key injuries have run rampant for the Pittsburgh Steelers over the past several weeks, and the team unfortunately saw another setback on defense in preparation for Week 6. We'll monitor Benton's status closely over the next several days, as his potential Week 6 absence would be a massive blow to a defense already missing defensive tackle Derrick Harmon. picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Rams -13.5 Moneyline: Rams -750; Cardinals +13.5 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Rams vs Cardinals expert picks Adam Kaufman: Rams 34, Cardinals 20 The Rams need a get-right game. Conveniently, the Cardinals are coming to town. Los Angeles has spent enough time trading punches with contenders. Now Matthew Stafford gets an Arizona defense that should provide a much friendlier afternoon, even with the shortened turnaround after Monday night. The Cardinals can move the ball through Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, and Jeremiyah Love gives the offense a reason to stay patient. I just don't see enough defensive resistance to keep the Rams from eventually creating separation, especially after the way they fell to the Bills . The concern is asking Los Angeles to cover a huge number after an overtime game. Winning this matchup feels considerably more straightforward. Give me Stafford, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Kyren Williams and enough explosive plays to put the Rams back in the win column. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Rams 38, Cardinals 20 Watch out, Arizona. The Rams might take out the frustrations of a 2-3 start on their divisional foe. The Cardinals haven't proven nearly capable of offering any resistance to an attack with as much firepower as Los Angeles, let alone stopping one. Maybe this isn't the game in which Carson Beck will make his NFL debut for Arizona as he looks to take on a role as more than a mere emergency quarterback, but a blowout might bring that possibility closer to reality. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Rams 31, Cardinals 16 Perhaps the Rams aren't the super team that we thought. A 2-3 start to the season certainly isn't doing the team any favors. However, Matthew Stafford looked like a quarterback that started to find himself again in Week 5 against the Bills. The Cardinals are the get-right team for every NFC West team that feels down about themselves. That's just the reality of being the doormat in a loaded division. Sean McVay's crew takes out all their frustrations on the lowly Cardinals, winning by a big margin to cover up all the special teams mistakes. away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. home.blurb: Quentin Lake is questionable due to a hip injury but Sean McVay said he's expected to play. It was described as a minor injury by the Rams coach. Lake is the only player who’s questionable for Monday night. The Bills, meanwhile, ruled out Ed Oliver and Joshua Palmer. Notably, D.J. Moore, the Bills’ top receiver, is questionable. Dee Alford and Landon Jackson are both questionable, as well. On Monday night, the Los Angeles Rams will get back three starters who missed last week's game against the Philadelphia Eagles . Aaron Donald, Colby Parkinson and Jaylen Watson are all good to go for Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills , which is a big lift for the Rams' offense and defense. Donald had been dealing with a back injury, while Parkinson missed Week 4 with shoulder and knee injuries. Watson dislocated his shoulder in Week 3 and missed the following week but he's back for L.A. The Rams and Bills square off on Monday night at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. home.headline: Rams designate 3rd-round rookie to return from IR
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are close to getting one of their top rookies back from injury. On Thursday, they designated Keagen Trost to return from injured reserve, officially opening his 21-day practice window. Trost has been out all season after injuring his hamstring in the first quarter of the preseason opener. He landed on IR during final roster cuts but could now be active for the first time on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. The Rams could use him, too. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams designate 3rd-round rookie to return from IR Now that the window has been opened, Trost can practice for the next three weeks. If the Rams wish to activate him from IR, they must do so in this 21-day window. If he's not activated by then, he will remain on IR all season. Alaric Jackson will miss one game due to a suspension , making David Quessenberry their starting left tackle. Trost will provide depth at both tackle spots in the event of an injury. Los Angeles drafted Trost in the third round this year. He finished his college career at Missouri in 2025, ranking as one of the best tackles in the country and earning All-American honors.

home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. Looking at the Chiefs' Week 6 matchup, Kansas City is taking on one of the worst teams in the league, record-wise. The Chargers are coming off their fifth straight loss, most recently at the hands of the Denver Broncos. Golden J starts this conversation praising LA's quarterback Justin Herbert, who he believes is still a great QB but has no supporting cast around him this season. With that being said, this is a game that the Chiefs should have zero issue winning. With the extra week of rest, dominant performances in the first four games, home-field advantage and a Chargers team that is seemingly completely hopeless, Kansas City is walking into a recipe for a win. With that said, the Chiefs can't overlook LA. The Chargers are still a professional football team and there's no situation where an NFL team can take its foot off the gas. Looking at the Chiefs' week off, the team did not sign or trade for an NFL-ready wide receiver despite Tyquan Thornton hitting the injured list with a dislocated ankle. Tight end Travis Kelce leads the team in receiving yards, but Thornton is a close second. There's hope that Thornton can return for the playoffs, but he'll be out for an extended period of time regardless. Head coach Andy Reid mentioned that rookie WR Cyrus Allen might be in the mix a bit more with Thornton's absence but the team does still boast a talented receiving corps consisting of Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and the Swiss Army knife of a TE, Kelce. Ex-Chiefs WR Tyreek Hill was initially believed to be back in KC, but his ongoing legal battle may complicate things. There hasn't been much on that front as of late, but a reunion is still on the table as long as he remains a free agent. Golden J and Chico breifly discuss a trade that could have been, with the Arizona Cardinals moving Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. Whether there was a possibility of Harrison landing with the Chiefs is unknown, but a thought to explore. Kansas City did bring on Justin Watson to their practice squad Monday, though there has been no subsequent move to elevate him to the game-day squad. Watson was previously with the Chiefs from 2022-2024, so he should be relatively familiar with their playbook.

home.headline: Chiefs’ WR injury woes could be fixed with one major trade
home.blurb: Knox recently named the Chiefs as a possible landing spot for disgruntled Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy, suggesting the Chiefs could send the Browns a conditional 2027 fifth-round pick in return. “According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, it’s ‘pretty well known around the league’ that Jeudy is available,” Knox wrote . “Per Schultz, the Browns would prefer to get a third- or fourth-round pick in exchange for the receiver, though that may be difficult. “The 27-year-old struggled through last season and has fallen out of the game plan this year as Concepcion, Boston, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. have become the go-to targets. Still, Jeudy is a talented pass-catcher who made the Pro Bowl just two years ago following a 1,229-yard season. His skill set hasn’t disappeared, and his 2026 base salary of $1.5 million should appeal to budget-conscious teams.” The Kansas City Chiefs have been pretty snake-bitten when it comes to keeping healthy wide receivers on their roster. Second-leading receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury nearly two weeks ago against the Las Vegas Raiders that will likely sideline him the rest of the season. Rashee Rice could miss some time with hamstring and knee injuries, and both Jeff Caldwell and Jimmy Holiday have been on injured reserve since the end of August. As things sit now, Xavier Worthy (14 catches, 133 yards, one touchdown), Jalen Royals (three catches, 17 yards, one TD), Cyrus Allen and Nikko Remigio are the only healthy WRs on Kansas City’s roster — and the latter two haven’t recorded a catch this season, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report thinks they should look to upgrade the position. Jeudy (eight catches for 81 yards in five games) has been almost a non-factor this season with the emergence of Boston and Concepcion. However, he had a 90-reception, 1,229-yard, four-TD season just two years ago. In Kansas City he would see much more than the three targets per game he’s currently getting in Cleveland. Jeudy would also give quarterback Patrick Mahomes the kind of reliable big-play target he’s been missing ever since the team traded away Tyreek Hill.
